say: Fondant shows every bump, so start with a firm ganache or buttercream coat, scraped sharp and chilled hard.

panel.heading: Cover a cake without pleats
items: Firm, smooth, chilled base coat
Roll: top + 2 x height + 5 cm
Roll 4 to 5 mm thick
Smooth the top, open the skirt
Trim, then weigh what you used

say: For example, Ebere in Abakaliki is covering a 20 centimetre cake, 12 tall. 20, plus 2 times 12, plus 5, means she rolls a 49 centimetre circle.

say: Roll to about 4 to 5 millimetres. Thinner tears. Thicker sags and cracks.

say: Drape it, smooth the top first to push out air, then lift the skirt with one hand and smooth down with the other.

say: Trim, then weigh the trimmings. Ebere used 820 grams, and wrote that down to cost her next cake exactly.
If a cold fondant cake sweats, do not wipe it. Let it dry in its closed box.

say: A celebration slice is about 2.5 by 5 centimetres, so 12.5 square centimetres. For example, Osas in Benin City planned three tiers. The 25 centimetre tier is about 491 square centimetres, which is about 39 servings.

panel.heading: Servings and support
items: Servings: tier area / 12.5
Take off about 10% for round tiers
Each tier on its own board
4 to 6 dowels, cut to the same height

say: All three tiers came to 78 in theory, or about 70 after cutting loss. For 150 guests, she added a kitchen sheet cake of the same flavour, cut behind the scenes.

say: Cake is soft. Without support, a top tier sinks. So every tier sits on its own board.

panel.heading: Servings and support
items: Servings: tier area / 12.5
Take off about 10% for round tiers
Each tier on its own board
4 to 6 dowels, cut to the same height

say: Push dowels into each tier that carries weight, mark them at cake height, cut them all the same, and push them back. The weight then passes through the boards to the drum, not the cake. Deliver chilled, boxed, flat, in a cool car.

say: Many skilled bakers stay busy but broke, because they price by guessing. Find the cost per gram of each ingredient: what you paid, divided by the grams in the pack. These prices are assumed, to show the method.

card.title: Pricing a 20 cm three-layer cake
card.note: Assumed prices. Use your own receipts.

say: Hauwa's ingredients come to about 12,000 naira. Butter is by far the biggest cost.

say: And her own labour, 5 hours at 1,500 naira an hour, which is 7,500. Total cost: 25,000 naira.

say: She adds a 30 percent markup, for a price of 32,500 naira. Her profit is 7,500, which is only about 23 percent of the price. So a 10 percent discount would cut her profit by over 40 percent. Offer added value before cutting the price.

say: Hot sugar goes well past 150 degrees and sticks to skin. Wear heat-resistant gloves and keep children out. If it touches skin, cool it under running water for at least 20 minutes, and get medical help for serious burns.

cards.d: Wear heat-resistant gloves. Children out. On skin: cool running water 20 minutes.
No wires or stems straight into cake. Use a posy pick and tell the customer.
Confirm money in your own bank app. Screenshots and text alerts can be fake.

say: Never push wires, toothpicks or flower stems straight into cake. Use a food-safe posy pick, and tell the customer what is not edible.

say: For every order, send a written brief and get it confirmed. Take a deposit, often 50 to 70 percent.
Label each cake with storage advice, a best-by date and allergens such as wheat, egg, milk and nuts.
And keep a weekly calendar, so you never accept more than your oven and hours allow.

say: To remember. Give fondant a firm base. Work out servings from the tier area. Support every tier with a board and dowels.
Cost ingredients, packaging, overheads and labour, then add profit. And remember, markup is not the same as margin.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Fondant needs a firm, smooth base
Servings: area / 12.5, minus 10%
Boards and dowels under every tier
Cost all five parts, then add profit
Markup on cost is not margin on price
